title: Choose the visual world for RoBorregos
question: The roll assigned the Rescue Maze field. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Rescue Maze Field
options.lineage: RoboCup Junior Rescue Maze, the league RoBorregos won its first title in (TMR 2015)
options.thesis: The site is a competition field the visitor explores tile by tile, the way the team's first robot did.
options.viewport: A top-down maze field fills the first viewport; the team photo and headline sit in open tiles while a small robot marker runs one exploration path from the entry tile to the Join and Sponsor tiles.
options.risk: Visitors who never saw Rescue Maze read the grid as abstract; the tile language must stay functional, not decorative.

raised.raise: Navigation keeps your trail: pages you have visited stay marked on the nav's tile strip, like the robot mapping explored tiles.
Selecting a filter or member isolates it and dims the rest instead of removing them, so the whole roster stays in view.
Every headline number traces to its source rows: tap a stat and the dated timeline entries behind it open.
One primary-action treatment (the checkpoint tile) used only for Join and Sponsor, everywhere else actions recede.
Each page is laid out along one axis of the field, with sections arriving as thresholds rather than stacked cards.

options.label: Borregos Game-Day Program
options.lineage: Tec de Monterrey Borregos varsity programs, rosters and jerseys
options.thesis: RoBorregos presented as a varsity program: roster, season record and robots as team entries.
options.viewport: Full-bleed team photo under a wide block wordmark, with a season-record strip of real dated results below.
options.risk: The most familiar choice: sports-team pages are a common look for university teams.

options.label: Endurance Livery Garage
options.thesis: The team's identity runs as a livery: stripe spine, number roundels and sponsor panels on every robot.
options.viewport: A robot shot as a car in the garage, the royal-blue stripe running nose to tail into the nav, sponsor panels gridded on the bodywork.
options.case: Sponsors read it instantly (logos on bodywork is sponsorship); loses on clarity because robots are not race cars.
options.risk: Reads as motorsport cosplay if the stripe system becomes decoration.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Every page a black-and-white card linked by painted buttons.
options.viewport: A fixed card with the team's name in a pixel menu bar.
options.case: Students and sponsors do not identify with 1987 Mac software; nostalgia hides the robots.
options.kept: The back-trail: visited pages stay marked in navigation.

options.label: Collider Event Display
options.thesis: The team as one frozen collision of tracks and energy.
options.viewport: A ring cross-section with members as tracks.
options.case: Near-black with signal accents is exactly the look you asked to drop; physics is not the team's field.
options.kept: Select-to-isolate: choosing an item dims the rest instead of hiding it.

options.label: Jacquard Brocade
options.thesis: Thousands of binary choices weaving one image.
options.viewport: A woven bird resolving from instruction rows.
options.case: Textiles carry neither audience nor the robots.
options.kept: Full traceability from the finished picture down to each instruction row.

options.label: Deco Cinema Lobby
options.thesis: Arrival staged as marquee, lobby and house.
options.viewport: A sunburst marquee over the team name.
options.case: Glamour reads wrong for a student engineering team.
options.kept: One primary-action frame reserved for the main action only.

options.label: Versailles Vistas
options.viewport: A palace axis receding into parterres.
options.case: Royal gardens have nothing to do with robotics or Monterrey.
options.kept: Measured sequence along one axis, sections as thresholds.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A university robotics team site the way most teams ship it, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Team photo hero with headline and two buttons, then project cards and sponsor logos.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other teams by design.
